_what: A HUMAN EYEBALL VERDICT on every recording in eval/frames/, recorded so the
denominator of any pass-rate is explicit and arguable. Made by reading
eval/sheets/*.jpg, NOT by asking the detector - selecting the test set with the
thing under test would make every survivor pass by construction.
Why it matters: the shipped accept rule is a >=6-of-8 frame CONSENSUS, which
assumes one fixed camera on one static court. Footage that breaks that premise
refuses for reasons that have nothing to do with surface, angle or corner
visibility, so pooling it into a single headline number would be misleading.
fixed      one fixed camera, one court - the product's actual input, and the
honest denominator for 'does court detection work'.
broadcast  one venue, MULTIPLE cameras (baseline cam, serve cam, close-ups).
The vote's premise is violated; a refusal is uninformative.
multivenue several different courts inside one file (a highlight compilation).
The vote CANNOT succeed - the frames are not the same court.

multivenue.uOy8ow5yoQ4: at least 5 distinct venues across its 8 frames (Cincinnati-ish blue/green, Shanghai purple, ATP purple, Tokyo blue-green). Excluded from every pass-rate.

surface_notes._why: Recorded because the brief targets clay and shell specifically, and the court GOLD set has one clay clip and no shell at all. These are eyeball surface calls on the drop set, not labels.

view_selection._what: Human ruling on WHICH camera angle of a cut recording is under test. Only the top-down view that shows the whole court is kept; half-court cameras, serve cams and close-ups are a different problem and pooling them measures nothing. Chosen from eval/sheets/pick_<clip>.jpg by eye, never by asking the detector.
